title: GREX-PLUS Science Book v1
extended_summary:
This paper is a science book / mission concept document for GREX-PLUS (Galaxy Reionization EXplorer and PLanetary Universe Spectrometer), a proposed cryogenic space telescope for JAXA’s strategic L-class program. It lays out the scientific motivation for the mission, emphasizing two broad aims: extragalactic science (especially the discovery of the first galaxies, the study of cosmic reionization, early black holes, dusty AGNs, and other high-redshift populations) and galactic/planetary science (including protoplanetary disk snowlines, interstellar molecules, exoplanet and Solar System atmospheres, and small bodies).

The paper describes the proposed instrumentation: a 1.2 m telescope cooled to 50 K, a wide-field imager covering 2–8 µm, and a high-resolution spectrometer covering 10–18 µm with resolving power around 30,000. It argues that the wide-field camera would enable deep, wide-area surveys capable of finding rare bright galaxies at very high redshift, while the spectrometer would enable velocity-resolved molecular studies impossible or difficult from the ground because of atmospheric absorption.

The intended scientific context is not a human participant study but an astronomy mission design and review document. For the extragalactic program, the paper highlights surveys of early galaxies, high-redshift quasars, submillimeter galaxies, and dusty AGNs; for the planetary program, it emphasizes locating water snowlines in protoplanetary disks and studying molecular lines in planetary and interstellar environments. The main conclusion is that GREX-PLUS would fill an observational niche not covered by existing or planned facilities, producing legacy data of broad importance for astronomy and astrophysics.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a mission science book / white paper describing a proposed space telescope and its anticipated astronomy applications, not an empirical K-12 study. It contains no evaluative research design, no student outcomes, and no intervention testing.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no measured educational impact on K-12 learners or institutions. The paper is unrelated to science inquiry supports in schooling and provides no evidence of effects by grade band, achievement, language background, or disability status.
